==== crux --help ====
A token-frugal CLI for the crucible controller API, and the MCP tool surface the controller hosts.

Usage: crux [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  whoami                Who the controller thinks you are, and how you got there
  playbooks             List registered playbooks: what `launch` can start
  playbook-caps         The admin caps on `--max-cost` and `--max-time`. Read before `launch` or `draft-launch`
  playbook-schema       The JSON Schema a playbook's params are validated against. Read before `launch`
  launch                Launch a playbook. Costs money against --max-cost
  playbook-runs         Playbook launches: key, playbook, status, count, cost against cap, and what stopped one
  playbook-run          One playbook launch whole, as JSON
  runs                  The runs leaderboard
  run                   One run with its candidates, as JSON
  schedules             Recurrences: what fires when, and whether each is enabled
  watches               Tracker watches: what each sweeps, and whether each is enabled
  watch                 One tracker watch, as JSON
  webhooks              Webhooks: what each launches, how it verifies, and when it last took a delivery
  webhook               One webhook, as JSON
  webhook-deliveries    A webhook's recorded deliveries, newest first, with how each settled
  provider-create       Register a provider from a JSON body (`POST /api/providers`)
  provider-update       Replace a provider's registration from a JSON body (`PUT /api/providers/<id>`)
  provider-delete       Deregister a provider and every default naming it. Refused while issues or schedules pin it; `provider-update` with `"enabled": false` retires one that work still names
  dispatch-defaults     The provider each scope's unpinned dispatches take, per workload class, and its fallback
  dispatch-default-set  Set one dispatch default from a JSON body (`PUT /api/config/dispatch-defaults`). Admin only
  webhook-check         Check a transform's CEL from a JSON body (`filter`, `dedupe`, `derive`) the way a save does. Prints `ok`, or fails with one `field:line:col: message` per refusal
  webhook-presets       Starting points for a webhook body: a sender's verifier and a transform, as JSON
  webhook-create        Create a webhook from a JSON body (`POST /api/webhooks`). Prints its secret, once
  webhook-update        Replace a webhook from a JSON body. Its verifier and secret stay as created
  webhook-resume        Resume a paused webhook: its address takes deliveries again
  webhook-pause         Pause a webhook: its address answers not found and its queued deliveries fail
  webhook-rotate        Replace a webhook's secret and print the new one, once
  webhook-delete        
  webhook-preview       Run a transform on a sample delivery from a JSON body; nothing is stored
  issues                List issues. One line each: key, status, tier, git ref, codegen contract, upstream, title
  issue                 One issue in full: provenance, the whole park reason, scopes, runs, and the event trail
  adopt                 Adopt a scenario: a controller issue with no upstream
  park                  Park an issue: stop working it, and record why
  unpark                Unpark an issue so the controller picks it up again
  bump                  Change an issue's priority. Higher runs sooner
  reconcile             Wake the controller's reconcile loop. A full pass, not one issue
  redispatch            Re-dispatch an issue's run. Costs money
  turns                 List work-pod turns
  turn                  One turn, with its result and error text intact
  graph                 A run's task graph in dependency order, each task with its latest status
  deployed              Which build the controller is running, and whether it is the commit you expected
  run-log               One window of a run's engine output, resumable by cursor
  run-files             The files a run's tasks captured: what the run produced, as opposed to what it narrated
  run-file              One captured file's content, by the key `run-files` listed it under
  contracts             The broker contract names this controller accepts
  approve               Approve a scenario or jira issue's scope pack
  approval-detail       One issue's approval gate: the PR to act on and the pack digest under it
  approvals             Every scope currently awaiting approval, plus the PRs already kept
  playbook-import       Propose a playbook pack import: fetch, compile, and store the preview an admin registers
  draft-files           A draft pack's files at one save, with the version a save must be based on
  draft-create          Create a draft pack in the authoring studio, from a template or a skeleton
  draft-save            Save a draft pack version from a `{path: content}` JSON map
  draft-pull            Write a draft pack into a directory, to edit it in your own editor
  draft-push            Save a directory back as the next draft version. The whole tree is the save
  providers             List the inference providers you may read: id, kind, default model, harness, the price per million tokens a run on it is charged, and whether launches may pick it
  secrets               List the secrets you own: id, name, kind, visibility, mode, owner. Never a value
  secret-create         Register a secret. The value is read from piped stdin, never from an argument or a terminal: `pbpaste | crux secret-create NAME --kind opaque`. Prints metadata, never the value
  secret-bind           Bind a secret to a draft, playbook, repo, or domain, so a run at that scope receives it. One scope flag and one projection flag
  draft-preview         What a draft version compiled to: its schema digest and diagnostics, without launching it
  draft-launch          Test-fire a draft's newest save. Costs money against --max-cost
  draft-delete          Delete a draft, every version of it, and its secret bindings, shares and schedules. Admin only; the id is free to create again
  draft-rename          Rename a draft. Its saves, secret bindings, shares, standing launches and launches follow
  draft-clone           Copy a draft's newest save into a new draft, with the bindings you could make yourself
  blueprints            List the blueprints you can read, with what each would carry for you and leave to bind
  blueprint-use         Start a draft from a blueprint. Bindings of the owning team's secrets carry when you are in that team; every other declared secret is a placeholder to bind with `secret-bind`
  blueprint-mark        Offer a registered playbook as a blueprint. Refused unless you may bind every secret whose binding would carry
  blueprint-unmark      Withdraw a blueprint, public or not. Drafts started from it keep what they carried
  blueprint-public      Let every user read and use a blueprint. Only its owning team's members get its secrets
  blueprint-private     Make a public blueprint private again
  draft-publish         Publish a draft: register its newest compiling version as a playbook, with no review
  draft-graduate        Graduate a draft: push its newest compiling version and open the export PR
  help                  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
==== crux -h ====
A token-frugal CLI for the crucible controller API, and the MCP tool surface the controller hosts.

Usage: crux [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  whoami                Who the controller thinks you are, and how you got there
  playbooks             List registered playbooks: what `launch` can start
  playbook-caps         The admin caps on `--max-cost` and `--max-time`. Read before `launch` or `draft-launch`
  playbook-schema       The JSON Schema a playbook's params are validated against. Read before `launch`
  launch                Launch a playbook. Costs money against --max-cost
  playbook-runs         Playbook launches: key, playbook, status, count, cost against cap, and what stopped one
  playbook-run          One playbook launch whole, as JSON
  runs                  The runs leaderboard
  run                   One run with its candidates, as JSON
  schedules             Recurrences: what fires when, and whether each is enabled
  watches               Tracker watches: what each sweeps, and whether each is enabled

  provider-create       Register a provider from a JSON body (`POST /api/providers`)

  -V, --version                Print version
==== crux whoami --help ====
Who the controller thinks you are, and how you got there

Usage: crux whoami [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help

          Playbook id

==== crux playbook-schema -h ====
The JSON Schema a playbook's params are validated against. Read before `launch`

Usage: crux playbook-schema [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Playbook id

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>        Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]
      --url <URL>              Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>  The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
  -h, --help                   Print help
==== crux launch --help ====
Launch a playbook. Costs money against --max-cost

Usage: crux launch [OPTIONS] --max-cost <MAX_COST> --max-time <MAX_TIME> <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          Playbook id

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --params <PARAMS>
          The params object its schema accepts, as JSON
          
          [default: {}]

      --max-cost <MAX_COST>
          Dollar ceiling for this launch

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --max-time <MAX_TIME>
          Wall-clock ceiling, e.g. 30m, 2h

      --dispatch-target <DISPATCH_TARGET>
          Cluster to dispatch onto. Omit for the controller's default

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Registered inference provider the run's agent talks to, replacing the pack manifest's `[agent]` harness. Omit to resolve through the configured defaults

      --model <MODEL>
          The model to ask that provider for. Needs --provider; omit for its default

      --rerun-of <RUN>
          Rerun this finished run of the same pack instead of starting afresh: every task it passed is reused, and the tasks --from names run again with everything after them

      --from <TASK>
          A task the rerun dispatches again, with everything downstream of it. Repeatable

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help
==== crux launch -h ====
Launch a playbook. Costs money against --max-cost

Usage: crux launch [OPTIONS] --max-cost <MAX_COST> --max-time <MAX_TIME> <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Playbook id

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]
      --params <PARAMS>
          The params object its schema accepts, as JSON [default: {}]
      --max-cost <MAX_COST>
          Dollar ceiling for this launch
      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
      --max-time <MAX_TIME>
          Wall-clock ceiling, e.g. 30m, 2h
      --dispatch-target <DISPATCH_TARGET>
          Cluster to dispatch onto. Omit for the controller's default
      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Registered inference provider the run's agent talks to, replacing the pack manifest's `[agent]` harness. Omit to resolve through the configured defaults
      --model <MODEL>
          The model to ask that provider for. Needs --provider; omit for its default
      --rerun-of <RUN>
          Rerun this finished run of the same pack instead of starting afresh: every task it passed is reused, and the tasks --from names run again with everything after them
      --from <TASK>
          A task the rerun dispatches again, with everything downstream of it. Repeatable
      --json
          
  -h, --help
          Print help
==== crux playbook-runs --help ====
Playbook launches: key, playbook, status, count, cost against cap, and what stopped one

Usage: crux playbook-runs [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --status <STATUS>
          

      --playbook <PLAYBOOK>
          

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help
==== crux playbook-runs -h ====
Playbook launches: key, playbook, status, count, cost against cap, and what stopped one

Usage: crux playbook-runs [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>        Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]
      --status <STATUS>        
      --playbook <PLAYBOOK>    
      --url <URL>              Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>  The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
      --json                   
  -h, --help                   Print help
==== crux playbook-run --help ====
One playbook launch whole, as JSON

Usage: crux playbook-run [OPTIONS] <KEY>

Arguments:
  <KEY>
          Issue key the launch became

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

  -h, --help

==== crux issues --help ====
List issues. One line each: key, status, tier, git ref, codegen contract, upstream, title

Usage: crux issues [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --kind <KIND>
          Input kind: github | scenario | jira

      --status <STATUS>
          Status: new | scoped | awaiting-approval | building | running | pr-open | parked | done

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Max rows. Default 50, applied client-side

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help

          Cut the issue body at this many chars
          
          [default: 6000]

      --config <CONFIG>

          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --json
          

      --url <URL>

==== crux adopt --help ====
Adopt a scenario: a controller issue with no upstream

Usage: crux adopt [OPTIONS] --title <TITLE> --repo <REPOS> --justification <JUSTIFICATION>

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --title <TITLE>
          

      --body <BODY>
          The ask, as prose. `-` reads stdin; otherwise it is a path to read

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --body-text <BODY_TEXT>
          The ask, inline. Use --body for anything longer than a sentence

      --repo <REPOS>
          A repo this touches. Repeat for several; the first is the clone target

      --justification <JUSTIFICATION>
          Why the controller should spend money on this

      --authoritative
          Treat the body as authoritative (skips grounded ranking)

      --git-ref <GIT_REF>
          Branch or tag to clone. Omit for the repo's default branch

      --codegen-contract <CODEGEN_CONTRACT>
          A configured broker contract (see `contracts`). Omit for local measure

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help
==== crux adopt -h ====
Adopt a scenario: a controller issue with no upstream

Usage: crux adopt [OPTIONS] --title <TITLE> --repo <REPOS> --justification <JUSTIFICATION>

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]
      --title <TITLE>
          
      --body <BODY>
          The ask, as prose. `-` reads stdin; otherwise it is a path to read
      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
      --body-text <BODY_TEXT>
          The ask, inline. Use --body for anything longer than a sentence
      --repo <REPOS>
          A repo this touches. Repeat for several; the first is the clone target
      --justification <JUSTIFICATION>
          Why the controller should spend money on this
      --authoritative
          Treat the body as authoritative (skips grounded ranking)
      --git-ref <GIT_REF>
          Branch or tag to clone. Omit for the repo's default branch
      --codegen-contract <CODEGEN_CONTRACT>
          A configured broker contract (see `contracts`). Omit for local measure
      --json
          
  -h, --help
          Print help

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --priority <PRIORITY>
          [default: 100]

      --reason <REASON>
          

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help

==== crux deployed --help ====
Which build the controller is running, and whether it is the commit you expected.

With --expect it is a gate: exits non-zero when the commit you named is not the one answering, so a deploy step can stop instead of reporting success it did not verify. Pass a full sha, e.g. `crux deployed --expect $(git rev-parse HEAD)`.

Usage: crux deployed [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --expect <EXPECT>
          The commit you expect to be running. Compared by prefix, so a short sha works

      --json
          

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

      --expect <EXPECT>        The commit you expect to be running. Compared by prefix, so a short sha works

==== crux run-log --help ====
One window of a run's engine output, resumable by cursor

Usage: crux run-log [OPTIONS] <RUN_ID>

Arguments:
  <RUN_ID>
          

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --cursor <CURSOR>
          Line to resume from, as the previous window's `cursor=` line reported it
          
          [default: 0]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Lines in this window. Capped at 200, which is also the default

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

  -f, --follow
          Keep printing new lines until the run is no longer running

      --interval <INTERVAL>
          Seconds between polls under --follow
          
          [default: 5]

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help

      --json                   
      --url <URL>              Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>  The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
  -h, --help                   Print help

Usage: crux playbook-import [OPTIONS] <REPO>

  <REPO>
          owner/repo or a clone URL

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --git-ref <GIT_REF>
          Branch or tag. Omit for the repo's default branch

      --path <PATH>
          The pack directory inside the repo. Omit for the repo root

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --variant <VARIANT>
          The `[variant.<name>]` of the pack's manifest to preview and register. Omit for the base manifest

          The registry id to propose registering under; prefills the review page

      --description <DESCRIPTION>
          The description to propose; prefills the review page

      --json

          Print help

Save a draft pack version from a `{path: content}` JSON map

Usage: crux draft-save [OPTIONS] --base-version <BASE_VERSION> --files <FILES> <DRAFT_ID>

Arguments:
  <DRAFT_ID>
          

Options:
      --base-version <BASE_VERSION>
          The version these edits were made against (see `draft-files`)

      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --files <FILES>
          The whole pack as a JSON object of path to content. `-` reads stdin

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --json

==== crux secret-create --help ====
Register a secret. The value is read from piped stdin, never from an argument or a terminal: `pbpaste | crux secret-create NAME --kind opaque`. Prints metadata, never the value

Usage: crux secret-create [OPTIONS] --kind <KIND> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>
          The name a pack's `[[secret]] name` refers to. Unique per owner

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --kind <KIND>
          [possible values: opaque, file, registry-authfile, kubeconfig, inference-api-key]

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --visibility <VISIBILITY>
          Omit for `broker-only`: the run gets it, the agent in the sandbox does not
          
          [possible values: broker-only, agent-visible]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --owner <OWNER>
          `user:<login>` or a `group:` in your claims. Omit to own it yourself

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help
==== crux secret-create -h ====
Register a secret. The value is read from piped stdin, never from an argument or a terminal: `pbpaste | crux secret-create NAME --kind opaque`. Prints metadata, never the value

Usage: crux secret-create [OPTIONS] --kind <KIND> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  The name a pack's `[[secret]] name` refers to. Unique per owner

      --config <CONFIG>          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]
      --kind <KIND>              [possible values: opaque, file, registry-authfile, kubeconfig, inference-api-key]
      --url <URL>                Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --visibility <VISIBILITY>  Omit for `broker-only`: the run gets it, the agent in the sandbox does not [possible values: broker-only, agent-visible]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>    The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
      --owner <OWNER>            `user:<login>` or a `group:` in your claims. Omit to own it yourself
      --json

==== crux secret-bind --help ====
Bind a secret to a draft, playbook, repo, or domain, so a run at that scope receives it. One scope flag and one projection flag

Usage: crux secret-bind [OPTIONS] <SECRET_ID>

Arguments:
  <SECRET_ID>
          The secret's id, as `secrets` lists it

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --playbook <PLAYBOOK>
          Scope: a draft or registered playbook id

      --repo <REPO>
          Scope: an `owner/name` repo

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --domain <DOMAIN>
          Scope: a domain id

      --env <ENV>
          Projection: the environment variable the value arrives in

      --file <FILE>
          Projection: the absolute path the value is written to

      --declared-name <DECLARED_NAME>
          The manifest's `[[secret]] name` this binding satisfies. Defaults to the secret's name

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help

      --playbook <PLAYBOOK>            Scope: a draft or registered playbook id
      --repo <REPO>                    Scope: an `owner/name` repo
      --url <URL>                      Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
      --domain <DOMAIN>                Scope: a domain id
      --env <ENV>                      Projection: the environment variable the value arrives in
      --file <FILE>                    Projection: the absolute path the value is written to

      --json

==== crux draft-launch --help ====
Test-fire a draft's newest save. Costs money against --max-cost

Usage: crux draft-launch [OPTIONS] --max-cost <MAX_COST> --max-time <MAX_TIME> <DRAFT_ID>

Arguments:
  <DRAFT_ID>
          

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]

      --params <PARAMS>
          The form values its schema accepts, as a JSON object of string to string
          
          [default: {}]

      --max-cost <MAX_COST>
          Dollar ceiling for this launch

      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870`
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]

      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody
          
          [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]

      --max-time <MAX_TIME>
          Wall-clock ceiling, e.g. 30m, 2h

      --schema-digest <SCHEMA_DIGEST>
          The schema digest these values were filled against (see `draft-preview`). A save that landed since is refused instead of launched

      --dispatch-target <DISPATCH_TARGET>
          Cluster to dispatch onto. Omit for the controller's default

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Registered inference provider the run's agent talks to, replacing the pack manifest's `[agent]` harness. Omit to resolve through the configured defaults

      --model <MODEL>
          The model to ask that provider for. Needs --provider; omit for its default

      --rerun-of <RUN>
          Rerun this finished run of the same pack instead of starting afresh: every task it passed is reused, and the tasks --from names run again with everything after them

      --from <TASK>
          A task the rerun dispatches again, with everything downstream of it. Repeatable

      --json
          

  -h, --help
          Print help
==== crux draft-launch -h ====
Test-fire a draft's newest save. Costs money against --max-cost

Usage: crux draft-launch [OPTIONS] --max-cost <MAX_COST> --max-time <MAX_TIME> <DRAFT_ID>

Arguments:
  <DRAFT_ID>  

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Config file. Defaults to `config.toml` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/crux` (else `~/.config/crux`), which may be absent; a path given here must exist. A flag or env var wins over the file [env: CONTROLLER_CONFIG=]
      --params <PARAMS>
          The form values its schema accepts, as a JSON object of string to string [default: {}]
      --max-cost <MAX_COST>
          Dollar ceiling for this launch
      --url <URL>
          Controller base URL: the API route. Defaults to a controller on this machine, `http://127.0.0.1:8870` [env: CONTROLLER_URL=]
      --api-token <API_TOKEN>
          The bearer: a minted `crk_` key, which authenticates as the person who minted it, or the controller's static token, which authenticates as nobody [env: CONTROLLER_API_TOKEN]
      --max-time <MAX_TIME>
          Wall-clock ceiling, e.g. 30m, 2h
      --schema-digest <SCHEMA_DIGEST>
          The schema digest these values were filled against (see `draft-preview`). A save that landed since is refused instead of launched
      --dispatch-target <DISPATCH_TARGET>
          Cluster to dispatch onto. Omit for the controller's default
      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Registered inference provider the run's agent talks to, replacing the pack manifest's `[agent]` harness. Omit to resolve through the configured defaults
      --model <MODEL>
          The model to ask that provider for. Needs --provider; omit for its default
      --rerun-of <RUN>
          Rerun this finished run of the same pack instead of starting afresh: every task it passed is reused, and the tasks --from names run again with everything after them
      --from <TASK>
          A task the rerun dispatches again, with everything downstream of it. Repeatable
      --json
          
  -h, --help
          Print help

==== crux help --help ====
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: crux help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  whoami                Who the controller thinks you are, and how you got there
  playbooks             List registered playbooks: what `launch` can start
  playbook-caps         The admin caps on `--max-cost` and `--max-time`. Read before `launch` or `draft-launch`
  playbook-schema       The JSON Schema a playbook's params are validated against. Read before `launch`
  launch                Launch a playbook. Costs money against --max-cost
  playbook-runs         Playbook launches: key, playbook, status, count, cost against cap, and what stopped one
  playbook-run          One playbook launch whole, as JSON
  runs                  The runs leaderboard
  run                   One run with its candidates, as JSON
  schedules             Recurrences: what fires when, and whether each is enabled
  watches               Tracker watches: what each sweeps, and whether each is enabled
  watch                 One tracker watch, as JSON
  webhooks              Webhooks: what each launches, how it verifies, and when it last took a delivery
  webhook               One webhook, as JSON
  webhook-deliveries    A webhook's recorded deliveries, newest first, with how each settled
  provider-create       Register a provider from a JSON body (`POST /api/providers`)
  provider-update       Replace a provider's registration from a JSON body (`PUT /api/providers/<id>`)
  provider-delete       Deregister a provider and every default naming it. Refused while issues or schedules pin it; `provider-update` with `"enabled": false` retires one that work still names
  dispatch-defaults     The provider each scope's unpinned dispatches take, per workload class, and its fallback
  dispatch-default-set  Set one dispatch default from a JSON body (`PUT /api/config/dispatch-defaults`). Admin only
  webhook-check         Check a transform's CEL from a JSON body (`filter`, `dedupe`, `derive`) the way a save does. Prints `ok`, or fails with one `field:line:col: message` per refusal
  webhook-presets       Starting points for a webhook body: a sender's verifier and a transform, as JSON
  webhook-create        Create a webhook from a JSON body (`POST /api/webhooks`). Prints its secret, once
  webhook-update        Replace a webhook from a JSON body. Its verifier and secret stay as created
  webhook-resume        Resume a paused webhook: its address takes deliveries again
  webhook-pause         Pause a webhook: its address answers not found and its queued deliveries fail
  webhook-rotate        Replace a webhook's secret and print the new one, once
  webhook-delete        
  webhook-preview       Run a transform on a sample delivery from a JSON body; nothing is stored
  issues                List issues. One line each: key, status, tier, git ref, codegen contract, upstream, title
  issue                 One issue in full: provenance, the whole park reason, scopes, runs, and the event trail
  adopt                 Adopt a scenario: a controller issue with no upstream
  park                  Park an issue: stop working it, and record why
  unpark                Unpark an issue so the controller picks it up again
  bump                  Change an issue's priority. Higher runs sooner
  reconcile             Wake the controller's reconcile loop. A full pass, not one issue
  redispatch            Re-dispatch an issue's run. Costs money
  turns                 List work-pod turns
  turn                  One turn, with its result and error text intact
  graph                 A run's task graph in dependency order, each task with its latest status
  deployed              Which build the controller is running, and whether it is the commit you expected
  run-log               One window of a run's engine output, resumable by cursor
  run-files             The files a run's tasks captured: what the run produced, as opposed to what it narrated
  run-file              One captured file's content, by the key `run-files` listed it under
  contracts             The broker contract names this controller accepts
  approve               Approve a scenario or jira issue's scope pack
  approval-detail       One issue's approval gate: the PR to act on and the pack digest under it
  approvals             Every scope currently awaiting approval, plus the PRs already kept
  playbook-import       Propose a playbook pack import: fetch, compile, and store the preview an admin registers
  draft-files           A draft pack's files at one save, with the version a save must be based on
  draft-create          Create a draft pack in the authoring studio, from a template or a skeleton
  draft-save            Save a draft pack version from a `{path: content}` JSON map
  draft-pull            Write a draft pack into a directory, to edit it in your own editor
  draft-push            Save a directory back as the next draft version. The whole tree is the save
  providers             List the inference providers you may read: id, kind, default model, harness, the price per million tokens a run on it is charged, and whether launches may pick it
  secrets               List the secrets you own: id, name, kind, visibility, mode, owner. Never a value
  secret-create         Register a secret. The value is read from piped stdin, never from an argument or a terminal: `pbpaste | crux secret-create NAME --kind opaque`. Prints metadata, never the value
  secret-bind           Bind a secret to a draft, playbook, repo, or domain, so a run at that scope receives it. One scope flag and one projection flag
  draft-preview         What a draft version compiled to: its schema digest and diagnostics, without launching it
  draft-launch          Test-fire a draft's newest save. Costs money against --max-cost
  draft-delete          Delete a draft, every version of it, and its secret bindings, shares and schedules. Admin only; the id is free to create again
  draft-rename          Rename a draft. Its saves, secret bindings, shares, standing launches and launches follow
  draft-clone           Copy a draft's newest save into a new draft, with the bindings you could make yourself
  blueprints            List the blueprints you can read, with what each would carry for you and leave to bind
  blueprint-use         Start a draft from a blueprint. Bindings of the owning team's secrets carry when you are in that team; every other declared secret is a placeholder to bind with `secret-bind`
  blueprint-mark        Offer a registered playbook as a blueprint. Refused unless you may bind every secret whose binding would carry
  blueprint-unmark      Withdraw a blueprint, public or not. Drafts started from it keep what they carried
  blueprint-public      Let every user read and use a blueprint. Only its owning team's members get its secrets
  blueprint-private     Make a public blueprint private again
  draft-publish         Publish a draft: register its newest compiling version as a playbook, with no review
  draft-graduate        Graduate a draft: push its newest compiling version and open the export PR
  help                  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
==== crux help -h ====
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: crux help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  whoami                Who the controller thinks you are, and how you got there
  playbooks             List registered playbooks: what `launch` can start
  playbook-caps         The admin caps on `--max-cost` and `--max-time`. Read before `launch` or `draft-launch`
  playbook-schema       The JSON Schema a playbook's params are validated against. Read before `launch`
  launch                Launch a playbook. Costs money against --max-cost
  playbook-runs         Playbook launches: key, playbook, status, count, cost against cap, and what stopped one
  playbook-run          One playbook launch whole, as JSON
  runs                  The runs leaderboard
  run                   One run with its candidates, as JSON
  schedules             Recurrences: what fires when, and whether each is enabled
  watches               Tracker watches: what each sweeps, and whether each is enabled
  watch                 One tracker watch, as JSON
  webhooks              Webhooks: what each launches, how it verifies, and when it last took a delivery
  webhook               One webhook, as JSON
  webhook-deliveries    A webhook's recorded deliveries, newest first, with how each settled
  provider-create       Register a provider from a JSON body (`POST /api/providers`)
  provider-update       Replace a provider's registration from a JSON body (`PUT /api/providers/<id>`)
